lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush’s ecstatic welcome after Elizabeth returns from church.

lines.text: Every day shows me more to love in you, dearest, and I open my arms as wide as I can ...
lines.note: Robert’s growing love and open-armed devotion.

lines.text: You asked me about Ossian—now here is truth—the first book I ever bought in my life was Ossian ... it is now in the next room.
lines.note: Robert’s childhood Ossian memory shows his private, bookish side.

lines.text: How I wish for two hearts to love you with, and two lives to give to you, and two souls to bear the weight worthily of all you have given to me.
lines.note: Elizabeth’s longing to give two hearts and two lives.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The shock of Flush being stolen in the street.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth compares Flush’s peril to her own among the banditti.

lines.text: This is the first time since we met at the beginning, that a whole week, from a Sunday to a Saturday, has gone by without a day for us.
lines.note: Robert marks the first full week without seeing her.

lines.text: The sight of your letter, even, did not provoke the cloud—that was only the lesser joy, I thought, preceding the greater!
lines.note: Elizabeth’s sudden turn from expected joy to grave news about Robert.

lines.text: I will go for a licence to-day and we can be married on Saturday.
lines.note: Robert proposes the licence and Saturday marriage.

lines.text: Dearest, I write one word, and have one will which is yours.
lines.note: Elizabeth gives her will to his and promises not to fail him.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth’s breathless account of the wedding day.

lines.text: All that I am, I owe you—if I enjoy anything now and henceforth, it is through you.
lines.note: Elizabeth credits Robert with lifting her into life and sunshine.

lines.text: Your letters to me I take with me, let the ‘ounces’ cry out aloud, ever so.
lines.note: Elizabeth insists on carrying Robert’s letters despite the ounces.
